title: The back gate is built: plan.gate becomes a list, the swarm's surprise mouth gets a door once the player has held it, and sentries can be ordered behind the bays
context: Owner, 2026-09-18: "Back gate is a reminder that focusing on defense on one side leaves one open; surprise it opens! Tank to the rescue + orbital + gunship. Then Isao installs a gate and we can put sentries." The last and largest of the 2026-09-16 known gaps (`2026-09-18-robustness-pass` left it deliberately unstarted): the back door stayed open once sector 2 cracked it, because the base could only ever have one gate. The single gate reached six places — the story base's gate mixer and open/close rule, base-print's gate plot, the pathfinder's gate rule in src/td-tab.js under its 13,505-line budget, the sector loop's gate integrity and pressure, Isao's repair orders and the HUD's GATE line.
outcome: src/domain/base-plan.js returns `gates`, entry 0 the front gate; `plan.gate` IS that same object, so every single-gate consumer reads what it read before and a plan built without a back mouth is otherwise byte-identical (test/base-plan.mjs deep-compares the two plans). A caller that passes `backMouth` (src/domain/back-door.js findBackMouth, which src/platform/story-world.js already computed) gets a second gate, always `pending`: it is never pre-built at any stage. Its cells are the WHOLE collapse, the mouth plus the flank rock that came down with it, and `plan.backSockets` are mounts on rock beside the back lane, found by walking the lane outward rather than taking the rock beside the mouth (that rock IS the flank and is gone once the mouth is down). src/fx/story-base.js keeps one record per gate — model, hydraulics clip, open radius, built flag — with base.gate()/growGate(k) unchanged for the front door and base.gateList()/gateSealed(id)/growGate(k, id) for the rest. story.sealed(ci) is a map lookup over the plan's gate cells instead of a comparison against one cell. src/fx/sector-run.js keeps one src/domain/gate-integrity.js per door, filling the map in as doors stand, presses each with the bodies nearest its own cells, and prints them side by side: GATE 100% · BACK 100%. src/domain/repair-orders.js takes a `gates` list and sends Isao to the worse door first (broken before chewed, lower share before higher, ties keeping the front door); a lone `gate` still means exactly what it meant. src/content/base-programme.js gains a tenth step, `backgate`: gate: 'back', no walls, its own plot, when { sector: 2, idle: true, back: 'held' }; src/domain/build-programme.js due() takes `back` and the host reads it off the sector loop's new backOpenBreaches(). Because the door is the one step a jumped-to stage cannot already have standing, story-world's standing() resolves a step's door by id (so it stays pending everywhere) and Isao's build loop lets that one step through on a base that otherwise prints nothing — which is what makes it reachable from ?skip=defence. Two lines from Isao (src/isaobriefs.js build_back_gate). src/td-tab.js unchanged at 13,505 lines: every edit was inside existing one-liners.
alternatives: Keeping plan.gate a single object and adding a parallel plan.backGate. Rejected: the sector loop, the repair rule and the HUD would each have grown a second code path for the same thing, and the owner's ask is that the second gate behaves exactly like the first.

Putting the back sockets straight into plan.sockets. Rejected: they would have been mountable from the first frame of every page, before the mouth is even cracked. They ride on plan.backSockets and join socketToward when the door is printed.

A door across the back mouth's two cells only. MEASURED AND REJECTED: the browser step caught thirteen bodies inside in forty seconds with the door standing — the collapse opens six cells and the swarm walked around the door through the four flank cells. The gate's cells are the whole collapse now.

Sockets on the rock immediately beside the mouth. Rejected for the same reason from the other side: that rock is the mouth's flank and comes down with it, so a mount there would stand on nothing. The lane walk finds rock further out (45954, 45953 on the shipped planet).

Testing the back gate under the sector's own waves. Rejected: sector 2 opens its own back-side breach, so backInside() counts bodies that never touched this door. The step keeps the sector quiet and puts one real back breach on the board.
evidence: npm test (120 test programs) and npm run check green on every one of the eight commits; the architecture guard holds src/td-tab.js at 13,505 lines throughout (net zero in all four commits that touch it).

test/base-plan.mjs: with no back mouth, gates.length 1, gates[0] === plan.gate, backSockets []; with one, the rest of the plan deep-equals the one-gate plan, the back gate is pending, on +Z against the front gate's -Z, carries the mouth plus the flank, and its sockets stand on rock aimed at the back lane and are in neither plan.sockets nor the gate's own cells.

test/repair-orders.mjs: two whole doors ask for no trip; the chewed back door is picked; the worse of two is picked and the front door carries no id; a broken door outranks a chewed one; doors come before walls; a tie keeps the front door first; repairsPending lists worst door first. One gate still reads exactly as it did.

test/build-programme.mjs: two gate steps, the front one with walls and the back one a wall-less door with a plot and when.back 'held', last on the programme; due() holds a when.back step while the back is untouched and while it is merely open, and releases it at 'held'.

scripts/browser-lock.sh node scripts/browser-test.mjs --back-gate, all steps PASS: on ?skip=defence the programme's only unprinted step is backgate with the front door standing and the back one not; the cracked mouth with no door on it is a way in; once the sector is 2 and the back is held Isao queues, flies and prints it; printed ['backgate'], perk on, gates [{gate,built},{back,built}], sector gates [{gate,60/60},{back,60/60}]; sealedAt() true on all six collapse cells; the back mounts join the sockets and a sentry is ordered on 45954; ninety seconds of a live 16-body back breach and zero of them inside on the back half, with the front door's hp untouched; breakGate('back') and they come through.

Screenshots looked at: artifacts/browser/back-gate-standing.png (the kit door standing on the back mouth, HUD SECTOR 2 · THE BACK DOOR · BREACHES 2 · WAVE 0/4 · GATE 100% · BACK 100%), back-gate-under-pressure.png (the swarm massed outside the closed door while the sentry on its mount fires on them), back-gate-printing.png, back-gate-socket.png, back-gate-down.png.

Regressions, all green after the change: --sectors (sector 2 secure, breaches A/gate/held 4of4 B/back/held 4of4), --backdoor (stage6 wallCount 43,015; collapse 6 cells, call 8.1 ms, no long tasks, max frame 22.9 ms against an 18.5 ms baseline; swarm inside), --grow (every step in order, Isao's gate repair 21.9 -> 60 hp), --skip-tutorial (secure, debrief, next sector), --defense (all steps).

NOT VERIFIED: the door opening for the tank is covered only by the shared code path — the same record, the same radius test in storyBase.tick — and by breakGate('back') proving that an open back door is a way through. No run drove a hull up to it. And the back door's wear under a real pile was not measured in the browser: sector-run gates pressure behind `quiet`, and the step keeps the sector quiet so the only bodies on the board are its own. The pressure rule itself is the front door's, unchanged, and is covered by test/gate-integrity.mjs and --sectors.
Reproduce through the lock only: /Users/minikai/Dev/stalheart/scripts/browser-lock.sh node scripts/browser-test.mjs --back-gate.
